extracted.intended_audience: government officials, civil society actors, and other stakeholders involved in developing OGP action plans and commitments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and evaluating Open Government Partnership (OGP) action plans and the commitments they contain, emphasizing co-creation with civil society, alignment with OGP values, and measurable, time-bound reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Action plans are at the core of a government’s participation in OGP. They are the product of a co-creation process in which government and civil society jointly develop commitments to open government reforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National action plans are typically implemented over two or four-year periods, while the implementation period of local action plans varies by member. Successful OGP action plans focus on significant domestic open government priorities and ambitious reforms; are relevant to the values of transparency, accountability, and public participation; and contain specific, time-bound, and verifiable commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-creation / Collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaboration between government, civil society and other stakeholders (e.g., citizens, academics, private sector) is at the heart of the OGP process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participating governments must ensure that a diverse set of stakeholders are engaged so that government and civil society jointly develop commitments. (Page notes co-creation as the defining production process for action plans.)

rubrics_metrics.name: OGP Commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: OGP commitments are promises for reform co-created by governments and civil society and submitted as part of an action plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitments typically include a description of the problem and concrete actions. They should be drafted to enable monitoring and assessment (i.e., specific, time-bound, and verifiable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance (open government lens)
rubrics_metrics.description: According to the OGP Articles of Governance, OGP commitments should include a clear open government lens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, commitments should advance at least one of the OGP values (for example: transparency, citizen participation, accountability). Relevance to domestic open-government priorities and ambitious reforms is a marker of a strong action plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiability
rubrics_metrics.description: OGP commitments should be clear and specific enough to enable measurement of their progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verifiable commitments include specific activities that can be monitored. Verifiability is a required quality so that implementation and progress can be tracked against the action plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency (as an OGP value)
rubrics_metrics.description: According to OGP’s Articles of Governance, transparency occurs when 'government-held information (including on activities and decisions) is open, comprehensive, timely, [and] freely available to the public.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency is one of the core values that commitments should advance; transparency-related commitments should therefore focus on making government-held information open, comprehensive, timely, and freely accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Participation (as an OGP value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Giving citizens opportunities to provide input into government decision-making leads to more effective governance, improved public service delivery, and more equitable outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitments and the co-creation process should create meaningful opportunities for citizen input; technical specifications and mechanisms for participation may be required to operationalize this value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating Governments (expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: OGP participating countries and locals – often referred to as OGP members – are committed to working with civil society to strengthen their adherence to open government values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership implies a commitment to the co-creation process and to producing action plans that conform to OGP standards (e.g., relevance to OGP values, specificity, time-bound targets, and verifiability).
